summary: Three well-written passages of real IELTS length (896, 893 and 839 words) whose difficulty rises properly from a history of the fork, to school gardens, to an argument about handwritten notes. Passage 3 is full IELTS difficulty, so the set is at the top of what B2 students should sit. One matching question had two correct answers and three Yes/No/Not Given items were out of passage order; both are now fixed.
strengths: Passage lengths and register match the real test: magazine/textbook style for a general reader, with C1 vocabulary and sentence structure in Passages 2 and 3.
A good mix of question types: sentence completion, T/F/NG, matching information, summary completion, matching people with one extra name, MCQ, Y/N/NG and a summary with a word box.
NOT GIVEN items are genuinely unaddressed (Q12 Sheffield vs Birmingham; Q31 recording lectures, with 'recorded talks' as a fair trap).
MCQ distractors in Passage 3 echo the passage's words while the correct option paraphrases it (Q27, Q29, Q30).
Completion answers are single words copied from the passage, in passage order.

issues.problem: Two defensible answers. 'an argument that gardens should not be judged by their effect on eating' fits paragraph D ('Diet may in any case be the wrong thing to measure') as well as the keyed F.
issues.change: Prompt reworded to 'a claim that gardens give pupils an experience unavailable elsewhere in their lessons' (only F: 'something the rest of the school day cannot supply'); key F kept; explanation and evidence updated.

issues.problem: Y/N/NG Q31-33 were out of passage order: Q33's text (recorded talks) is in paragraph 1, and Q32's evidence (2019 study) comes before Q31's (narrowed claim) in paragraph 3.
issues.change: Swapped the statements, keeping numbers and type: Q31 is now the recorded-lectures item (NOT GIVEN), Q32 'firmly confirmed' (NO), Q33 'writing by hand can sometimes help memory' (YES). Answer pattern is NG, NO, YES, YES, NO, with no runs of three.

issues.problem: Paragraph E ('almost every abandoned garden had lost that teacher') also gives a reason gardens are given up. 'In the past' points to B, but a weaker student may hesitate.
issues.change: Optional: 'the historical reasons why school gardens declined after the mid-twentieth century'.

issues.problem: 'speed' in the word box is a weak rival to 'tool' ('the decisive factor is not the speed itself'), since handwriting's slowness is part of the argument.
issues.change: Acceptable as it stands ('tool ... itself' matches 'Neither implement'). Could replace 'speed' with an unrelated word, e.g. 'volume'.

issues.problem: Several Passage 1 completion prompts lift the passage's wording almost unchanged (Q1 'expected to bring their own', Q2 'condemned by the', Q4 'ground round'), which makes Passage 1 easier than the rest.
issues.change: Suggest paraphrasing the stems, e.g. Q1 'Diners at medieval feasts had to supply their own ______', Q2 'Churchmen known as the ______ criticised the princess'.

issues.problem: Broken paraphrase pairs: Q1 ['supplied the food', 'provided'], Q4 ['blade', 'knife'], Q6 ['within reach of', 'brought within reach'], Q22 ['money for replacing tools', 'budget'], Q39 'wider connections' and Q40 'the tool' did not appear in what the student reads. Q13 ['a rejected sample', 'discovery'], Q17, Q32 and Q34/35 pairs were not real paraphrases or had opposite meanings.
issues.change: All replaced with pairs copied from the passage and the question (e.g. Q13 ['on the problem of erosion inside gun barrels', 'investigating an unrelated problem'], Q25 ['written into the school timetable and the budget', 'part of its ordinary business']).
